//exports: ONE public entry point, and it ships no code (11-electron.md §4): 'Typed

The `types` condition is the ONLY one, deliberately. A subpath with no runtime
target cannot be imported at runtime — Node and every bundler fail the resolve
with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED rather than pulling an Electron app into a
browser bundle. That is the 01-architecture.md §2.3 rule ('apps are not imported')
enforced by the resolver instead of by review.
The root '.' is absent for the same reason: this app is not a library. Electron
loads `main` by absolute path (it never resolves @adminium/desktop as a
specifier), so `main` and `exports` are not in competition here.
NOTE — no package depends on this one, and none may: @adminium/desktop#build
dependsOn @adminium/dashboard#build (turbo.json), and turbo builds its graph
from `dependencies` AND `devDependencies`. A dashboard → desktop package edge
would therefore close a task cycle and every `turbo run` in the repo would fail.
@adminium/dashboard consumes this contract through a tsconfig `paths` mapping to
this exact file instead — a type-only edge with no package edge. See the note in
//scripts: `build` chains the offline asset gate because 11-electron.md §7 says it 'runs
in CI on every desktop build' — and the only way to make that literal, rather
than a workflow step someone can forget to keep next to the build, is to make
it part of the build. It scans out/renderer + out/dashboard, which do not
exist until electron-vite has run, so this is also the earliest point it CAN
run. The root `pnpm check-offline-assets` script is the same check as a named
CI step (matching check-deps); both are wanted.
//packaging: 11-T13. `dist`/`pack` are the ONLY call sites of electron-builder.yml — a
config no script runs packages nothing. They are NOT turbo tasks: turbo's
cache keys off file inputs, and a real electron-builder run downloads Electron
binaries and (on mac) reads signing certs from the environment, neither of
which is a hermetic input turbo can hash. The release workflow (11-T14) drives
the full sequence explicitly, in order:
1. build   — electron-vite bundles out/**, generates NOTICES, offline-gate
2. icons   — derive resources/icons/* from the master (needs the sharp +
icon-gen devDeps; see below). electron-builder.yml points
mac/win/linux .icon at these files, so this runs BEFORE dist.
3. dist    — electron-builder: npmRebuild the native addons for Electron's
ABI (in apps/desktop/node_modules — see //native-modules),
then sign/notarize/package.
`pack` (--dir, no installers, no signing) is the fast local smoke: it proves
the app dir assembles, without the dmg/notarize cost.
NO LONGER TRUE (2026-08-14): `pack`/`dist` used to leave the pnpm-shared
better-sqlite3/argon2 addons built for Electron's ABI, so locally they had to
be followed by `pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3 argon2` at the repo root or the
rest of the repo's tests went red. Both addons are Node-API now (better-sqlite3
>= 13, argon2 >= 0.44), and an N-API binary loads under Node and Electron
alike — so there is no incompatible ABI left to strand the shared copy in. The
restore is harmless but unnecessary; see apps/desktop/README.md 'Packaging
locally' and the header of electron-builder.yml.
`sharp` and `icon-gen` are DECLARED devDependencies below (build-only):
the release workflow runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which installs
only what the lockfile already carries — it can neither `pnpm add` on the fly
nor would --frozen-lockfile permit it — so the `icons` step's `loadDesktopDep`
resolve of each from apps/desktop MUST find them already linked here. They are
not runtime deps of the shell and no `src/` file imports them; only
scripts/make-icons.mjs (repo root) reaches them, via a require anchored at this
package.
//dependencies: RUNTIME DEPS OF THE FORKED SERVER (11-electron.md §2.1/§3), not of the shell.
electron.vite.config.ts bundles @adminium/server into out/server/index.js, but
a bundler cannot inline a module reached through a COMPUTED specifier, and it
must not inline a native one. Those stay runtime `import`s — resolved by Node
against the IMPORTING file (out/server/index.js), i.e. against THIS package's
node_modules, never against apps/server's. So every one of them is declared
here even though no line of apps/desktop/src imports any of them. Verified by
resolving each from out/server/index.js; a miss is silent at runtime, which is
what makes the list load-bearing rather than decorative:
@adminium/adapter-{postgres,mysql,sqlite} — connections/register-adapters.ts
loads these by name from ADAPTER_PACKAGES and CATCHES the failure into
`missing: []`. Undeclared, the desktop app boots a complete API and then
cannot open a database of any engine — including the local SQLite the whole
product is built on — with no error anywhere but a debug log. Their own
header states the rule: declared deps of whichever package hosts the entry
file, 'so they resolve inside the deployed image and not just in a
workspace checkout'. out/server/index.js is a new such artifact.
better-sqlite3, argon2 — native (.node). argon2 is a static external; the
meta store reaches better-sqlite3 via `importDriver`. §2.1 required these
rebuilt against Electron's ABI with @electron/rebuild; both are Node-API as
of better-sqlite3 13 / argon2 0.44, so they load under Electron unrebuilt
and the packaging note above no longer describes a hazard. They still MUST
be declared here — an undeclared native dep is unresolvable at runtime
regardless of which ABI it was built for.
pg, mysql2 — OPTIONAL, mirroring apps/server's own note. The desktop meta
store is ALWAYS local SQLite (§2.1), but a SOURCE db may be a reachable
Postgres/MySQL, and meta/store.ts reaches those drivers the same way.
This is a DEPLOYMENT surface, not an import edge: 01-architecture.md §2.3 caps
what apps/desktop/src may IMPORT at @adminium/server, and .dependency-cruiser
`desktop-shell-only` enforces exactly that against the source graph.
//native-modules: NATIVE ABI: @electron/rebuild MUST NOT be wired into a `postinstall` here,
and this note is why — the instruction in 11-electron.md §2.1 ('wired into
`postinstall` for `apps/desktop` and into electron-builder's `npmRebuild`')
predates the pnpm layout and its first half is not safely expressible in it.
pnpm gives the whole workspace ONE better-sqlite3: apps/server, apps/desktop,
apps/e2e, packages/meta and packages/adapter-sqlite all symlink to the same
node_modules/.pnpm/better-sqlite3@<v>/node_modules/better-sqlite3. That part
is still true and is why a postinstall here would be reaching into shared
state rather than its own.
THE ABI HAZARD THAT ORIGINALLY FORBADE IT IS GONE (2026-08-14). The argument
used to run: prebuild-install resolves a single
build/Release/better_sqlite3.node, electron-rebuild rewrites that file in
place, so a postinstall here would compile the SHARED copy against Electron's
ABI (148 for Electron 43) and every Node-side suite — running at the local
Node's ABI (127 on Node 22) — would fail to dlopen it, turning root `pnpm
test` red for everyone on every install.
Two things changed. better-sqlite3 13 dropped prebuild-install entirely and
migrated to Node-API, shipping prebuilds inside its own tarball and preferring
them over build/Release. argon2 0.44 is likewise N-API (napi_versions: [8],
resolved by node-gyp-build, which prefers build/Release but produces an N-API
binary either way). An N-API addon is ABI-stable across Node and Electron by
construction, so there is no longer an ABI in which a rebuild could strand the
shared copy.
THE CONCLUSION STILL HOLDS, on weaker grounds: no `postinstall`. It would do
pointless compile work on every install for everyone, for a rebuild whose
output better-sqlite3 does not even load. The rebuild stays where it is, in
electron-builder's `npmRebuild: true` (11-T13), together with §10's
`asarUnpack: ['**/*.node']` — and asarUnpack is NOT optional at any ABI: a
.node inside an asar cannot be dlopen'd.
WHERE npmRebuild RUNS — corrected 2026-07-21, still accurate. This note and
electron-builder.yml both once justified the choice by claiming `npmRebuild`
operates on a STAGED, private node_modules. It does not: app-builder-lib forks
@electron/rebuild with `buildPath: appDir`, and appDir is apps/desktop itself,
so it walks the SAME shared store described above.
The local restore that used to be required afterwards —
`pnpm rebuild better-sqlite3 argon2` at the repo root — is obsolete. Harmless
to run; nothing breaks without it. See apps/desktop/README.md ('Packaging
locally') and electron-builder.yml's header.
Packaging out of a `pnpm deploy --filter @adminium/desktop` tree (a real,
non-symlinked node_modules) behind a beforeBuild hook would make the isolation
literal. It is now a tidiness follow-up rather than a correctness one.
THE DEV-LOOP CONSEQUENCE IS ALSO GONE. This note used to warn that until
11-T13 landed, `pnpm --filter @adminium/desktop dev` forked a utilityProcess
on Electron's bundled Node and the meta store's better-sqlite3 import threw
ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED (NODE_MODULE_VERSION mismatch), surfacing as
{ type: 'error', stage: 'meta-store' } on the crash screen. 11-T13 has shipped,
and the N-API bumps removed the mismatch independently. @electron/rebuild
remains declared here for the packaging path.
